The term property can represent the information associated with an entity.
It is not limited only to variables or attributes.
In the context of inheritance, the properties and behaviors available in the parent class can become available to the child class through the inheritance relationship.
Single inheritance occurs when one class inherits from one parent class.
Multilevel inheritance occurs when inheritance exists through multiple levels.

21. What are the six types of inheritance?
In the Java class-inheritance model covered here, single, multilevel, hierarchical, and hybrid inheritance are permitted, while multiple and cyclic inheritance are not permitted.

25. How can hybrid inheritance be represented in Java?

26. What happens when multiple inheritance is attempted using Java classes?
Multiple inheritance attempts to make one class inherit from more than one parent class.
The class-inheritance model in Java does not permit a class to extend multiple classes.
An attempt to represent this structure should be compiled so that the resulting compiler error can be examined.
27. What happens when cyclic inheritance is attempted?
Cyclic inheritance creates a circular relationship between classes.
This means a class eventually becomes part of its own inheritance chain.
Java does not permit this type of inheritance.
A program containing the circular extends relationship produces a compiler error.
28. Why are compiler errors useful when testing unsupported inheritance structures?
A compiler error identifies that the inheritance structure cannot be represented in the specified form.
For unsupported structures, the error can be examined to understand the restriction.
This approach can be used particularly for multiple and cyclic inheritance.
29. What topics are associated with inheritance in Java?
These topics describe how methods, constructors, keywords, and object references behave within inheritance relationships.

class can use the properties and behaviors available from the parent class.

The child class can acquire properties and behaviors from the parent class.
